plates.want: At peace in one's own company (PD)

beats.text: Five Stoic lessons on being alone — without being lonely.
One. Solitude is where you finally meet yourself. The Stoics sought it on purpose.
Two. If you can't enjoy your own company, no amount of other people will ever fill the gap.
Three. Marcus said: men seek retreats in the country — but none is calmer than retreating into yourself.
Four. A crowd is no cure for loneliness. Depth is. One real connection beats a hundred shallow ones.
Five. Become whole on your own, and company turns into a choice — never a desperate need.
The Stoic is never truly alone. He always has the one companion he's worked hardest to respect: himself.
